Your mission, Martians, is to swoop down on the pathetic denizens of the primitive planet Earth and scoop up as many of the inhabitants as you can manage. We are interested in samples of the Chicken, Cow, and Human populations so that we can determine which of them is actually in charge. The Earthlings might manage to put up a feeble defense, but surely nothing that a small taste of your Death Rays can't handle. Make Mars proud – be the first Martian to fill your abduction quota! In Martian Dice you will roll 13 custom dice in an effort to set aside ("abduct") Humans, Chickens, and Cows. With each roll you must first set aside any Tanks, representing the human military coming to fend off your alien invasion. Then you may choose one type of die to set aside as well - one of the earthlings to abduct, or Death Rays to combat the military. At the end of your turn, if you have at least as many Death Rays as Tanks, then you may abduct the earthlings you've been setting aside. You can't pick any type of Earthling twice in one turn, but if you manage to abduct at least one of each you'll score a bonus! With each roll you will ask yourself, do you feel lucky? Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary For tips on how to play martian dice, see Tips_MartianDice Contents 1 Theme 2 How to play 3 Scoring 4 Game End Theme Your mission, Martians, is to swoop down on the pathetic denizens of the primitive planet “Earth”, and to scoop up as many of the inhabitants as you can manage. We are interested in samples of the Chicken, Cow, and Human populations, so that we can determine which of them is actually in charge. The Earthlings might manage to put up a feeble defence, but surely nothing that a small taste of your Death Rays can’t handle. Make Mars proud... be the first Martian to fill your abduction quota! How to play Every Turn is divided into Rounds Every Round, players roll dice and set some of them aside. Rounds follow the following structure: 1. If there are no available dice to roll, your Turn is over; proceed to Scoring. Otherwise, roll all of the available dice. 2. Humans Attack: Set aside all Tanks, adding them to any Tanks set aside earlier this Turn. (In BGA, this is done automatically for you.) 3. From the remaining dice, set aside as many or as few as you want. Choose one type, following these rules: a) Abduction: Chickens, Cows, or Humans. Set aside all dice of the chosen type. Note that Chickens, Cows, or Humans may not be chosen if you have already set that type aside this Turn. b) Defence: Death Rays, these may always be chosen and are added to any Death Rays set aside earlier this Turn. 4. If you cannot set aside any dice based on these restrictions, your Turn is over; proceed to Scoring. Otherwise, continue. 5. End of a Round: You may choose to end your Turn and proceed to Scoring, or return to step 1 to continue rolling. The dice : Each die features 1 Tank, 2 Death Rays, 1 Human, 1 Cow, and 1 Chicken. Scoring First, compare the number of Tanks set aside to the number of Death Rays set aside. If there are more Tanks than Death Rays, you must flee without any abductees; you score zero points for the round, regardless of how many other dice you set aside. If you set aside at least as many Death Rays as Tanks, then you have successfully fended off the Earthling military and will score points for your abductees as follows: 1 Point for each Human, each Cow, and each Chicken that you set aside. 3 bonus points if you set aside at least one of all three Earthling types. Record your score and pass the dice to the next player. Game End The game end is triggered when one player reaches a total score of 25 points or more. Once this happens, the round is completed so that all players have had the same number of turns. At the end of that round, the player with the most points wins the game! [Rating: 1/10] Doesn't offer much more than other Yahtzee variants, and I don't generally like Yahtzee or its variants.

[Rating: 1/10] 2012 Golden Geek Best Party Board Game Nominee 2012 Golden Geek Best Children's Board Game Nominee

[Rating: 1/10] Absolutely brainless game. Too long and too boring. Just a waste of time even if you play it on BGA.

[Rating: 2/10] Beautiful dice, dumb game. 100% luck. Get King of Tokyo instead for dice chucking fun. For a fast filler, there are lots of other better games.

[Rating: 2/10] Almost on par with phase 10 in terms of "gameness" in that there isn't much of a game to be played here.

[Rating: 2/10] Grałam w Martian Dice na board game arena i to była zła decyzja. Gra jest tak dziwna, w opór losowa, nie sprawia żadnej przyjemności. Nie chcę w to więcej grać. Zraziła mnie do siebie. Jedyna fajna rzecz to customowe kosteczki :)  Ocena po 1 partii w 3 osoby. Czas gry = 12 min.  bga

[Rating: 2/10] Forgettable dice game. Not necessarily offensively bad, it's just that there are much better options to play instead.

[Rating: 3/10] Martian Dice is strictly for children.  Despite the clever theme (abducting humans and cows and chickens, oh my!) this is Yahtzee with far less strategy.  It almost plays itself.

[Rating: 3/10] 120102 If this is the available PYL game I'd certainly play it, but it tries to be too thinky for what it is.  I prefer zombie dice.

[Rating: 3/10] John Weber roped me into trying this one. (I wanted to play 7 Wonders.) I do not like most dice games, and this proved to be no exception. Just a bunch of rolling dice and deciding on which ones to keep, hoping your virtuous Martian Green Death Rays outnumbered the Evil Red Human Tanks, and scoring one or two points in the bargain. I fared poorly in my game because the dice hated me (they often do). I didn't like them much either so I guess we're even. Takes too long for what it is, which is not much at all.

[Rating: 3/10] Components: Nice sized dice with clear iconography. Fun theme.  Experience: Senseless but mildly amusing. I wouldn't recommend this with more than two players, as adding more players doesn't add any enjoyment for the existing players, but does create more down time between turns. As Yahtzee-style games go, there are much better games out there.  Eagerness to Play Again: No Desire  Plays (1): 4 players: 1

[Rating: 3/10] I generally like dice games, but this one isn't really up to snuff.  Play Roll through the Ages or King of Tokyo.  This one doesn't really have any decision making or anything else of interest going on.
